review.operatorWide: Hawaii By Storm reports 4.9 on Google (456), 5.0 on TripAdvisor (369), 4.9 on Yelp (47) and 100% recommend on Facebook (53) as of October 15, 2026.

verdict.intro: This is the most demanding and most expensive of Hawaii By Storm's tours, and it only makes sense for a full vehicle of fit travelers with a single day who want both Waimoku Falls and a Haleakalā sunset; at 7 guests it is about $243 each before tax. The hike-then-climb sequence means 12 or more hours and a temperature drop of 30°F or more after a sweaty trail. Groups with two days should book the Waimoku Falls tour ($1,399.95) and the Haleakalā Summit tour ($1,399.95) separately and sleep in between.

faq.q: How much is the Pīpīwai Trail and Haleakalā summit tour?
faq.a: The Pīpīwai Trail and Haleakalā summit tour costs a flat $1,699.95 per Luxury Expedition SUV for up to 7 guests, plus 4.712% Hawaii GE tax, on hawaiibystorm.com as of October 2026. Greetwell resells the same tour at $1,882.05. The price is per vehicle, not per person.

faq.q: How long is the Pīpīwai and Haleakalā combo tour?
faq.a: The combo tour is listed at 12 hours by the operator and Greetwell, covering the Kaupō back road, a 3–4 hour Pīpīwai Trail hike, a food stop and the climb to the Haleakalā summit for sunset. Greetwell's review summary says the operator's full-day tours often run 12 to 13 hours.

faq.q: Is park entry included for both Haleakalā districts?
faq.a: Yes, Hawaii By Storm includes Haleakalā National Park entry for both the Kīpahulu district, where the Pīpīwai Trail begins, and the summit district, per its tour page. A Yeti cooler with ice and drinks and door-to-door pickup are also included; food and gratuity are not.

faq.q: Can non-hikers join the Pīpīwai and summit tour?
faq.a: Non-hikers can join; Greetwell's listing says guests must be able to walk short distances but may stay at the vehicle while others hike. The operator's Waimoku Falls page adds that guests who do not finish the hike can wait at the Kīpahulu visitor center.

faq.q: How cold is the Haleakalā summit at sunset?
faq.a: The Haleakalā summit at 10,023 feet can be 30°F or more colder than the Maui coast, with wind and cloud arriving quickly, according to Hawaii By Storm's tour page. The operator's packing list calls for warm layers, a jacket and long pants for the sunset portion.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for this tour?
faq.a: Hawaii By Storm refunds in full with 7 or more days' notice, 50% with 4 to 6 days' notice and nothing with 3 days or less; no-shows pay in full, per its policy page and the Greetwell listing checked in October 2026. Greetwell also charges $100 for rescheduling within 24 hours of the tour.

faq.q: How much is the Hawaii By Storm Haleakalā summit private tour?
faq.a: The Haleakalā summit private tour costs a flat $1,399.95 per Luxury Expedition SUV for up to 7 guests, plus 4.712% Hawaii GE tax, on hawaiibystorm.com as of October 2026. The price covers the vehicle, guide, park entry, pickup and drinks; it is not a per-person rate.

faq.q: Does the Haleakalā summit tour include sunrise?
faq.a: No, Hawaii By Storm's Haleakalā summit tour offers daytime and sunset departures only, per its tour page. Sunset departures end at Keoneheʻeheʻe Overlook. Travelers who want sunrise, which requires a separate National Park Service reservation, need a different operator or a self-drive.

faq.q: How long is the Haleakalā summit tour?
faq.a: The Haleakalā summit tour lasts 6 to 8 hours, per the operator's page, including pickup, a Kahului provisioning stop, the drive through Kula, Hosmer Grove, the visitor center, the overlooks and the 10,023-foot summit. Daytime departures add a 1.8-mile loop walk when conditions allow.

faq.q: Is there hiking on the Haleakalā summit tour?
faq.a: Daytime departures include the 1.8-mile Halemauʻu Overlook Loop walk, subject to access, weather, time and group ability, plus a short walk at Hosmer Grove to look for native birds. Sunset departures skip the loop walk. The operator does not state an overall difficulty rating.

faq.q: How cold is the summit of Haleakalā?
faq.a: The summit of Haleakalā can be 30°F or more colder than the Maui coast, with wind and cloud that arrive quickly, according to Hawaii By Storm. The operator's packing list asks for warm layers or a jacket, long pants for sunset, comfortable walking shoes and sun protection.

faq.q: What is the cancellation policy for the Haleakalā summit tour?
faq.a: Hawaii By Storm refunds in full with 7 or more days' notice, 50% with 4 to 6 days' notice and nothing with 3 days or less, per its policy page checked in October 2026. No-shows are charged in full. Cancellations must be made by phone at (808) 444-3770; rescheduling is allowed subject to availability.
